findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a gallon of whole milk at an ambient temperature of 50F in one of the infant room refrigerators. The gallon of milk (which had been in the room for over 24 hours), as well as an individual bottle of milk (brought in 2 hours ago) probed at an internal temperature of 47F. CORRECTED- the gallon of milk was voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Milk bottles were moved into refrigerators observed to be properly cold holding. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Refrigerator in an infant room was observed at an ambient temperature between 48-50F. Inspector turned down the cooling setting from 1-.05. Unit was observed to be at the same temperature 20 minutes later. The equipment is failing to hold TCS items at or below 41F (see violation #22). Ensure TCS items are held in working cooling units until this item is serviced. Inspector will return on 11/12/25 to ensure the refrigerator has been serviced to cold hold at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed one cooling unit in an infant room to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- PIC moved a thermometer into the cold holding unit. Ensure all cold holding units holding TCS items contain an ambient thermometer, placed in the warmest part of the unit, to monitor cold holding temperatures. Staff should monitor cold holding units to be at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
One Food Handler card was observed to have been expired 11 days ago. Ensure all staff obtain a Food Handler’s license within 30 days of hire, and maintain this certificate to be renewed every 3 years. A Food Handler’s course helps to ensures safe food handling practices.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a probe thermometer available for use in the kitchen. Ensure probe thermometers are available and calibrated to check internal food temperatures.
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 PIC at time of inspection was chewing gum while working in the kitchen. Gum was discarded at request of inspector. Ensure staff are not eating while working in in the kitchen, including chewing gum and/or eating candy.
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee helping with dishes entered the kitchen after exiting the restroom and did not wash hands prior to removing a clean pot from the dish machine. Hands were just washed in the restroom but need to be re-washed upon entering the kitchen prior to handling clean equipment and/or working with food because door knobs were touched to exit the restroom and enter the area leading to the kitchen. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. Ensure hands are consistently and properly washed between tasks as needed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, upon entering the kitchen, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet and handle to paper towel dispenser were both touched between washing hands and getting paper towels to dry hands. Handwashing process also happened relatively quickly and lasted less than a total of 20 seconds. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and educational handout was provided. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee helping with dishes was observed washing hands at the 3 part sink. Proper handwashing at designated handwashing sinks was discussed. Handwashing sink was used to wash hands prior to continuing with the next task. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Kitchen manager adjusted their face mask and did not wash hands prior to continuing with lunch prep. Manager was later observed handling a personal beverage container to add water and took a drink/touched straw up near mouth and did not wash hands before walking back toward the stove to continue with lunch prep. In both instances handwashing was discussed resulting in hands being immediately washed. Ensure hands are consistently and properly washed between tasks as needed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands (touching cell phones and face masks, etc.).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Three cartons of raw shell eggs were stored on the top shelf of the 3 door cooler directly above cheese. Proper storage of raw shell eggs was discussed. Cartons were moved to the bottom of the cooler beneath all ready to eat foods.  
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-204.112 Thermometer was not present the fridge located in toddler room 206. Ensure functioning thermometers are present in all classroom fridges.
Cold holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14 Employee left the kitchen to retrieve food carts from rooms. Upon returning to the kitchen hands were not washed prior to removing clean dishes from the dish washer. Handwashing was discussed with staff. Employee washed hands prior to handling any more clean dishes. 

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the kitchen and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.11  (P) Food employee hands and exposed portions of arms are not clean. Instructed food employee to wash hands and exposed portion of arms. Reference 2-301.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Bleach solution was observed at 100ppm. The label directions show a required concentration of 200ppm. Solution was just prepared recently and not yet used. More bleach was added to bring the solution to proper concentration of 200ppm.

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at proper concentration based on label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Stem of the digital food thermometer was soiled with grease. Manager noted she typically uses the other non-digital stem thermometer. French toast was served for breakfast, and cooking temperature was not checked. Cleaning frequency for food thermometers was discussed. Both thermometers were to be cleaned and sanitized prior to checking temperatures during lunch prep.
 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. Stems may be wiped with sanitizer solution before and after temperature checks during prep and must be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle of yellowish color liquid was not labeled as to the contents. Chlorine test strip was bleached out. Kitchen manager verified the liquid was straight bleach used as a working supply for preparing solutions. Bottle was labeled as to the contents.

Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Metal stem thermometer was reading below 60°F at ambient temperature. Manager stated it had been awhile since the thermometer was last calibrated. When checked in ice water solution the thermometer was reading close to 20°F. Pliers were used to properly calibrate the thermometer to 32°F in the ice water solution. The digital food thermometer was also checked and observed at 33°F and considered calibrated. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.

Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) front of oven door/handle (food splash);
B) drip tray under burners (splash/food debris);
C) dish machine - general surfaces including top and inner edges along top of doors (general buildup);   and
D) lower shelf of prep table across from warmer (dust/general buildup). 
Clean the aforementioned items.

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee entered the kitchen and began to put away clean dishes without first washing her hands. When reminded of handwashing upon entering the kitchen, the employee did a quick handwash that lasted less than 10 seconds and did not do proper technique. Proper handwashing was discussed, and hands were re-washed properly before putting away any more clean dishes.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, upon entering the kitchen, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Kitchen staff were observed washing hands without proper technique. Bare hand contact occurred with the handle of the manual faucet and the paper towel dispenser once handwashing was completed. Proper handwashing was discussed with kitchen staff. Step by step poster is located at the kitchen handsink.
Staff were observed washing hands properly for the remainder of the inspection.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and before working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1320 - Spray bottles in rooms 201 thru 206 were all observed to be stronger than 200ppm chlorine. Test strips were consistently getting bleached out. Dilution of solution was discussed with staff in rooms 201-206. Inspector did not visit any other rooms and spoke with kitchen staff that typically make the bulk bleach solution used to fill the classroom bottles. CFM was advised on using test strips to verify the concentration is no stronger then 200ppm. CFM noted she did not make the solution today but would inform other staff of proper concentration and use of test strips.

Toxics must not be used in a manner that poses a threat of cross contamination to food or surfaces and/or a health hazard to persons exposed to and/or using the chemical. Follow the label instructions, and use test strips to verify the concentration is maintained at 150ppm (no stronger than 200ppm) per label instructions.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Ravioli and green beans in pots on the stove had internal temperatures ranging from 114°F-130°F. Ravioli portioned and held in the top of the warmer had an internal temperature of 118°F while green beans portioned and held in the bottom of the warmer had an internal temperature of 176°F. Kitchen manager stated the final cooking temperature for beans and ravioli was 165°F and portioning for hot holding in the warmer began around 845a. A significant amount of food portions for the classrooms were stacked within the warmer. That in combination of being in and out during prep/portion process may have resulted in temperature loss for items higher up in the warmer. Also, the ravioli was portioned more recently to inspector's arrival and may have had some temperature loss prior to being placed in the warmer. Remaining portions of foods on the stove would be portioned for any staff that wanted them. Foods on the stove were to be reheated prior to service, and all portions of food in the warmer would be served or discarded before 1p. Any additional leftovers would be discarded.

Hot time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be maintained at 135°F/above at all times during storage, display and service. The exception to this being if there is a time control policy that is actively being followed by staff (see general comments).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
(R) 750.810 - Sani-buckt in the kitchen was at ~50ppm chlorine. Solution was prepared earlier that morning and was ready to be changed.

Maintain bleach solution at 200ppm (per label instructions). Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.800b - An accumulation of metal shavings was observed in the crevice around the can opener blade.

Clean and sanitize the can opener between uses/up to every 4hrs after continuous use, and be mindful of the area around the blade where grease and metal shavings can accumulate.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Portion of vegetarian rice for lunch was observed in a tupperware container in the bottom of the specialty milk fridge in the kitchen. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 72F-79F and 100F respectively. Date and time were not indicated on the container. Manager noted the product was placed in the fridge around 9a because a small metal bowl was not available for storage in the warmer. The rice was to be served by 11a. Manager was advised the cooling process was in progress due to storage. When a similar situation occurs in the future it would be a better practice to hold a food hot on the stove until it is time for lunch service or hold the product at room temperature (labeled with time of prep/portioning) and use or discard w/in 4hrs.
If foods are cooling they need to be cooled properly and labeled with date and time.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.160 - Improper glove use was observed. Employee put on oven mitts over her gloved hands to remove a tray of biscuits from the oven; single use gloves were not changed prior to handling biscuits. Employee was advised the inner surface of oven mitts are not considered a clean surface and gloves needed to be changed. Proper glove use/changing gloves between tasks and handwashing between glove changes were discussed. Hands were washed prior to obtaining a new pair of gloves to continue with food handling.

Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations. Always properly wash hands before putting on gloves and between glove changes.
Educational handouts on handwashing and glove use were provided.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckt in the kitchen was at 0ppm chlorine. Solution was prepared earlier that morning and was ready to be changed.

Maintain bleach solution at 200ppm (per label instructions). Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - An accumulation of metal shavings was observed in the crevice around the can opener blade.

Clean and sanitize the can opener between uses/up to every 4hrs after continuous use, and be mindful of the area around the blade where grease and metal shavings can accumulate.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Bleach solution in a spray bottle was observed to be slightly stronger than 200ppm chlorine (test strip was very dark in color with some clear spots). Bleach bottles are filled daily from a bulk solution that is made fresh each day and dated. Kitchen staff are the ones that typically make the solution and fill the bleach bottles for the rooms. Kitchen Manager was advised on preparation of bleach solutions and use of test strips to verify the concentration.

Maintain bleach solution in the bulk container and spray bottles at 100-200ppm. Use test strips to ensure the bleach solution is at proper concentration.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250  The mini-fridge holding special milks is observed holding temperature at 49F. Milks from the front of the cooler and the back were probed. Milk in the front lower shelf was found to be 50F and milk from the back was found holding temperature at 48F. Milk was discarded during the inspection. Cooler was turned to coldest setting. The hanging thermometer read just under 50F. Monitor the temperature of this cooler prior to restocking with specialty milks. Continue to monitor daily. There is an additional cooler in the kitchen that can hold specialty milks. All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 The wall behind the dry storage shelving in the water main room is observed to have water damage/mold on the wall (look low and to the right of the baker's rack). Kilz this portion of  the wall to insure water damage/mold doesn't move up the wall. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) There is not a thermometer available in Room 206. Also, discussed checking periodically with rooms to insure that mini-fridges are being monitored for temperature. It is suggested that you have staff educated about proper cold holding temperatures. All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed employee not wash hands prior to donning gloves and after touching facility door knobs and equipment. Handwashing was discussed and completed. Make sure that hands are washed between activities. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b The red sani-bucket in the kitchen tested at under 100 ppm Cl in solution. During the inspection, bleach was added to the bucket. Test strips are available. Make sure that sani-bucket is checked after water is added to dilute bleach solution. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1210 The wall to the right of the mop sink is damaged (crumbling drywall). Also, the wall behind the rolling island in the kitchen has damage from constant hitting. Repair the wall by the mop sink. Seal and repair the wall behind the island - install a suitable bumper to protect the wall from future damage. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
750-1210e The hood over the oven is observed dusty. There is no service sticker available. Make sure that hood is getting routinely serviced and cleaned.   Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily cleanable and shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 Observed a piece of coving on the right side of the mop sink to be missing. The present drywall is damaged. Replace the missing section of coving and repair the visible wall. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 The caulking of the kitchen handsink is starting to crack. Reseal the sink to the wall. Also, watch the wall behind the stainless steel island adjacent to the handsink. The metal island hits against the wall causing damage to the drywall. Make sure that drywall dust and paint are smooth and do not pose a physical contamination problem to food and equipment stored on this space. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750- 1300: Observed a spray bottle of bleach to be entirely too strong (strip bleached out). During the inspection, almost the entire contents of the bottle were rinsed out in order to achieve the proper concentration of 100ppm Cl. If using a spray bottle to sanitize surfaces test the concentration to insure 100ppm Cl is reached. Only a drop of bleach is needed for the entire bottle of water. Make sure that staff knows to test the concentration using available test strips.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-830 Observed dishmachine to not be testing for proper chlorine residual. Machine was primed multiple times and still detemined to 0ppm Cl. Operators and staff are unaware of who maintains the equipment. For today, facility is going to sanitize in third sink (50ppm Cl for 60 seconds). Spot check late next week. Test machine daily to insure adequate sanitizing. All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Cloth used for wiping of roll carts is not stored in sanitizer bucket of solution between uses. Staff is using spray bottle to sanitize carts. During inspection, bucket was created and cloth stored within. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed pipe beneath the garbage grinder to be soiled with food and mold. Observed hood to be soiled with accumulation dust around exhaust and sides. Clean the pipes and hood. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) REPEAT: There are still two upright coolers in the infant rooms that are not supplied with thermometers. Supply each cooler with thermometer. Make sure staff is educated to monitor temperatures -especially within the mini-fridge. Two thermometers are needed or the two coolers in the infant wing. Temperature should be maintained at 41F or below. All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-130(d) Observed raw eggs stored over cheese slices, milk, and other ready-to-eat foods in the upright cooler in the kitchen. During inspection, a gallon of milk was moved and the eggs were properly stored on the lowest shelf in the cooler. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 The handsink in the kitchen is not properly caulked to the wall. Caulk and then smooth the caulking so sink to wall gap is eliminated. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-800b Observed well over 200ppm Cl in an unlabeled spray bottle. Test strip turned black. Discussed sanitizing with staff. Emptied bottle almost completely twice in order to obstain a proper concentration of 100ppm Cl. Spray bottles used to wipe down food contact surfaces should be tested at 100ppm Cl. Dishmachine is also bleach and should test at 50ppm Cl. To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Observed unused bowls and utensils being stored in the dry storage room under the sprinkler system. See variance request . Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750-1300 Observed two spray bottles to be labeled with manufacturers generic mark of 'disinfectant'. One spray bottle contained bleach at well over 200ppm Cl (see violation #20a above) the other bottle contained vinegar water. During the inspection, spray bottles were properly labeled with contents. Bleach marked as sanitizer. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
